candidates.title: Man who used fraudulent passport to get in and out of Canada 16 times handed 2-year sentence
candidates.description: A Ghanaian man who used a fraudulent Canadian passport to leave and re-enter the country 16 times has been sentenced to two years in prison for citizenship fraud.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canadian ultramarathoner Stephanie Case is the 1st woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica
candidates.description: Canadian ultramarathoner Stephanie Case completed the Antarctic Ice Ultra in Queen Maud Land, Eastern Antarctica, on Sunday, making her the first woman to run 100 miles, or 160.9 kilometres, on the southernmost continent covered by the largest ice sheet in the world.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Stellantis signs deal to sell Brampton, Ont., assembly plant to Canadian armoured vehicle maker
candidates.description: Canadian armoured vehicle maker Roshel Inc. will buy the Stellantis assembly plant in Brampton, Ont., the automaker announced Monday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk does a Q&A (and a backflip) from space
candidates.description: Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk answered questions from students in St. John's and showed off life in zero gravity from aboard the International Space Station on Monday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ottawa doubles maximum time employer can hire low-wage temporary foreign workers
candidates.description: The government said restrictions on hiring temporary foreign workers in cities with unemployment rates above six per cent will remain in place. But Ottawa is adding early childhood educators to the list of professions exempted from those restrictions, which already includes certain jobs in health care, construction and food processing.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ontario university student pleads not guilty in U.S. court amid Chinese 'espionage' probe
candidates.description: An Ontario university student has pleaded not guilty in a U.S. federal court in a case a prosecutor described as involving "espionage-type activities." Weiheng (Billy) Zeng is charged with making false statements following an FBI counter-intelligence investigation.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Payments Canada launches long-delayed instant payments system
candidates.description: Payments Canada says it has launched its real-time rail national payment system, which is expected to speed day-to-day payments for Canadian businesses and consumers.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Mental state of Steven Galloway's accuser detailed at ongoing defamation trial
candidates.description: Galloway is suing his accuser and other defendants, alleging they defamed him by publishing unproven claims on social media and elsewhere.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Honda Canada announces plans to retool Alliston, Ont., plant for hybrid production
candidates.description: Honda Canada says it will retool its manufacturing facilities in Alliston, Ont., to expand production of hybrid-electric and gasoline-powered vehicles. The Japanese automaker announced Monday it is partnering with the federal and provincial governments to fund plant upgrades, including the reintroduction of engine manufacturing, with an initial $166-million investment.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Some women in Canada are choosing fertility treatments to avoid passing down genetic mutations to their kids
candidates.description: Egg freezing is surging in Canada and genetic testing is one of the motivations. We spoke with a woman planning to freeze her eggs so she can test her embryos for the BRCA 1 gene mutation.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Red Deer, Alta., wins bid to host the 2028 Brier men’s national curling championship
candidates.description: Central Alberta curling fans have a big upcoming event to celebrate in 2028. The Brier is set to return to Red Deer, Alta., for the first time in more than three decades. In Red Deer Monday, Curling Canada announced that the 2028 Montana’s Brier will be hosted in the city from Feb. 25 to March 5, 2028.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada's secretary of sport questions Russia competing as neutrals at Alberta world juniors
candidates.description: Adam van Koeverden, Canada's Secretary of State for Sport, has cast doubt on whether Russia can compete as a neutral team at the upcoming world junior hockey championship in Alberta.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: B.C. Conservatives gain 1 more seat, kicking out incumbent NDP MLA in Burnaby after final count
candidates.description: Conservative candidate David Xie has snatched the Burnaby South-Metrotown riding from NDP incumbent Paul Choi, winning by 64 votes, following the final vote count.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Man pleads guilty to manslaughter in Saskatoon homicide sparked by missing drugs
candidates.description: Edin Vrazalica's trial for first-degree murder was scheduled to begin Monday. Instead, he pleaded guilty to manslaughter in the February 2024 death of Lee Perkins in Saskatoon.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Heated Rivalry could be getting 2 more seasons and a movie, sources say
candidates.description: Deadline has reported the cast and crew of Heated Rivalry are currently filming not one but two new seasons, and a movie could be scheduled for theatrical release in December 2027.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ford calls students protesting OSAP changes 'naive,' says they should be 'thanking the government'
candidates.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford called students who protested Ontario Student Assistance Program changes and tuition hikes "naive" on Monday — likening them to "sheep" who blindly follow "looney tunes" on social media.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Drug possession is illegal. Why can people use openly in public?
candidates.description: The drop in prosecutions — and the apparent rise in open usage — coincides with a Public Prosecution Service of Canada policy change in 2020 directing prosecutors away from laying criminal charges for drug possession, according to police officials and experts who spoke with CBC News.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Parents warned extremist groups are targeting a growing number of kids online across Prairies
candidates.description: Violent extremist groups are grooming, recruiting and radicalizing a growing number of children and teenagers across the Prairies, police and researchers say.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Suspicious tree removal and permits linked to Toronto developer
candidates.description: A Toronto developer is facing new accusations of illegal tree removal at a residential property in Etobicoke. Four trees were recently cut down without permits at a property connected to Modcity. The company denies any wrongdoing.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Inuvik killed dozens of grizzly bears at a dump this summer. Experts say it may have been the kindest option
candidates.description: This summer, over 28 grizzly bears were shot in Inuvik. While some people are now wondering why the Department of Environment has to ‘dispatch’ problem bears, instead of relocating them or leaving them alone, experts say death may be the kindest option.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: U.S. House Republican moves to force vote on impeaching Pete Hegseth
candidates.description: Republican Rep. Thomas Massie moved Monday to force a vote to impeach Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, putting pressure on his fellow Republicans to decide whether to remove one of the Trump administration's most prominent figures following sweeping election losses.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump downplays FBI probe into Nvidia chief's affair with alleged spy
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said Monday that the FBI is investigating Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese government agent, but said he doesn't think the executive who has helped to develop artificial intelligence has a reason to worry.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Tyler Robinson, man accused of shooting Charlie Kirk, to face trial in 2028
candidates.description: A ​Utah judge on Monday set a June 2028 trial date for Tyler Robinson, the man accused of murdering prominent right-wing activist Charlie Kirk last year.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What these newly elected U.S. reps. think about tariffs on Canada
candidates.description: Several newly elected Democratic representatives are calling for an end to the U.S.-Canada trade war, citing concerns over rising living costs and job losses.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is embroiled in a spying scandal. Could the AI chipmaker survive without him?
candidates.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has helmed the company since starting it in 1993, guiding it from a graphics card maker to the AI behemoth it is today. But with an investigation now underway into whether Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort and no clear successor in sight, analysts say a change at the top — if it were deemed necessary — would be massive.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Fact check: Is this a photo of the Poland shooter?
candidates.description: The Polish gunman who killed six people in Krakow has been identified as 24-year-old Michal Oksinski. But is that the person shown in this photo circulating online? CBC’s Fact Check team debunks the misinformation.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 2026 Booker Prize goes to post-apocalyptic, sci-fi novel The End of Everything
candidates.description: English author M. John Harrison has won the 2026 Booker Prize for his novel The End of Everything, a post-apocalyptic adventure that explores what it means to be human in a shifting world. It's the first time a science fiction writer has won the annual prize, which honours the best novel written in English.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Nvidia's shares slide as chip giant probes CEO Jensen Huang over spy claims
candidates.description: Nvidia shares tumbled in early trading on Monday after an internal investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort put his future at the AI chipmaker under scrutiny.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Judge clears way for Lindsay Clancy to face potential 2nd trial
candidates.description: A Massachusetts judge cleared the way on Monday for Lindsay Clancy to be tried again on murder charges for killing her three young children at her home in 2023, saying a retrial would not unconstitutionally subject ‌her to a double prosecution for the same crime.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: France blames Iran for cyberattack that hacked supermarket refrigerators across the country
candidates.description: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot ‌on Monday accused Iran's ​Revolutionary Guards of being ​behind a recent cyberattack ​on French supermarket fridges, saying ‌there would be consequences for the country.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Like father, like son: Arnold Schwarzenegger’s son muscles into top 5 at bodybuilding competition
candidates.description: More than 60 years after Arnold Schwarzenegger first flexed his stuff on a bodybuilding stage, his youngest son is continuing the dynasty of muscle, scoring in the top five during his professional debut over the weekend.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Woman, 3 children killed in Gaza after sand embankment collapses onto tents
candidates.description: Torrential rain in Gaza caused a sand embankment to collapse onto tents, killing a woman and three small children in an incident that highlighted the danger facing hundreds of thousands of displaced Palestinians as the rainy winter season sets in.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Russell Brand sentenced to more than 10 years in prison on convictions for rape, sexual assaults
candidates.description: Comedian Russell Brand, once one of ‌Britain's most high-profile broadcasters and briefly a motion picture star, was sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in prison on Monday after being convicted for rape and three sexual assaults.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: $276 for hair ties? Skims offers advent calendar refunds after online backlash
candidates.description: After intense customer backlash, Kim Kardashian's apparel brand Skims is offering refunds to anyone who purchased its 2026 accessories advent calendar, which costs $276 and was advertised as "12 fun days of surprises."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Lionel Messi achieves MLS first, winning Golden Boot for second straight season
candidates.description: Lionel Messi has been awarded the 2026 MLS Golden Boot, becoming the first player in league history to win the award in consecutive seasons.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: James Gunn, Peter Safran out of DC Studios as Skydance shakeup continues
candidates.description: Skydance Motion Picture Group announced Monday that James Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down as co-chief executives after four years leading DC Studios.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Russia's top independent newspaper closes under relentless government pressure
candidates.description: Novaya Gazeta, Russia's most celebrated independent newspaper, closed its Moscow offices Monday, citing relentless pressure from government officials.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Polish police say Krakow mass shooting assailant died in hospital
candidates.description: A young gunman who killed six people in central Krakow on ‌Saturday in Poland's unprecedented mass shooting has died in hospital, police said early ​on Monday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Death toll rises to 39 after migrant boat capsizes off Senegal
candidates.description: The death toll from the capsize off Senegal of a boat carrying migrants rose to 39 following the discovery of more bodies on Monday, the country's emergency services said.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Roshel to buy Stellantis assembly plant in Brampton for undisclosed amount, automaker says
candidates.description: Canadian armoured vehicle maker Roshel Inc. will buy the Stellantis assembly plant in Brampton, Ont., the automaker announced Monday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Top U.S. hedge fund executive named CEO of Canada's new sovereign wealth fund
candidates.description: A top executive at one of the world's largest hedge funds is leaving her job in the U.S. to become the CEO of one of the Carney government's hallmark projects.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Kids clothing company Children's Place files for bankruptcy, plans to sell assets
candidates.description: Founded in 1969, Children's ​Place said it has more than 500 stores in the United States and Canada. The company said its stores and e-commerce sites remain open, and says its in talks with multiple groups about a potential sale of its assets.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Nvidia probes whether CEO Jensen Huang targeted by foreign intelligence as he admits affair
candidates.description: Top Republican lawmakers ​in the U.S. House of ​Representatives have called on Jensen Huang to brief Congress this month about a New York ​Times report in October alleging he had a close relationship with a ‌Chinese businesswoman who passed information to Beijing.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: How Trump's tariffs are threatening to spoil the success of Canadian cheese
candidates.description: In recent years, Canadian cheese has been having a bit of a moment south of the border, taking home some of the biggest awards in the Western hemisphere. But Trump's 50 per cent tariffs on certain dairy products, including Canadian cheese, are threatening to spoil this success.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Poilievre pans Liberal budget's $15M capital gains exemption, calls for 'simpler' plan
candidates.description: Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre is criticizing a key feature of the Carney government's latest budget, arguing the proposed $15-million capital gains exemption on the sale of qualifying shares from a Canadian company applies too narrowly, excluding key businesses.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump says FBI investigating Nvidia boss's affair with alleged Chinese spy
candidates.description: The US president said he spoke with Jensen Huang on Monday and asked him about the affair with the alleged spy.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Ukraine peace talks resume with 'some flexibility' by warring sides, US officials say
candidates.description: Kyiv, Washington and Moscow are all sending delegation to the United Arab Emirates for the first trilateral talks since February.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking
candidates.description: Tons of chilled and frozen food was spoiled last month as fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets heated up.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Republican congressman to force impeachment vote on Defence Secretary Hegseth
candidates.description: The effort will likely fail, but Representative Thomas Massie wants to push Trump to fire Hegseth before Democrats can launch their own impeachment process next year.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Russia's leading independent newspaper closes after eviction
candidates.description: The outlet has been evicted from its offices of three decades and says it's been blocked from receiving donations.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Turkey steel factory blast kills at least 17 people
candidates.description: Eyewitnesses say the explosion shook the ground, with one believing an earthquake had hit near the Habas Demir Celik plant in Aliaga.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Trial date of alleged Charlie Kirk killer set for June 2028
candidates.description: Tyler Robinson has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder and six other charges in connection with the 2025 killing of the conservative activist.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Krakow shooting suspect has died in hospital, police say
candidates.description: Six people were killed in the shooting, and three bodies of the suspect's family members were found at their home.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Cruise ship pianist rescued from sea after nine hours in Pacific Ocean
candidates.description: Two US fishermen say they spotted the man treading water around 20 miles (32km) off the Californian coast.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Dana White declines Trump’s offer to be White House press secretary
candidates.description: In a social media post over the weekend, the president asked the UFC boss to take over the role, but later said he was "having a little fun".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Millions fill Buenos Aires streets to welcome Pope Leo XIV
candidates.description: The Pope celebrated an outdoor Mass in Argentina's capital, the second stop on a 12-day tour of Latin America, just three weeks after having had surgery for lung cancer.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Rare insight into France's drug gangs recruiting children to commit violence
candidates.description: "It destroys people, but we all make our own choices" - Marseille drug-gang members spoke to the BBC.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: What do we know about Nvidia CEO’s affair with a suspected Chinese spy?
candidates.description: Adoration for the US tech giant’s CEO Jensen Huang has been labelled “Jensanity”, but can his reputation survive the news of his affair?
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'I treat all these people like they are victims', says doctor who treated Krakow shooting suspect
candidates.description: Two doctors were eating near the Polish city's Main Market Square when a gunman began firing at random.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Footage shows derailed carriages after fatal train crash in Egypt
candidates.description: At least seven people died when two trains collided, causing several carriages to derail and fall down an embankment.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: The superpower battle over energy – and what it means for your bills
candidates.description: A tug-of-war between China and the US could have a big impact on energy costs, but who will win?
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Zoe Kleinman: Nvidia CEO's affair will cause ripples across US and beyond
candidates.description: Jensen Huang is being investigated by his own company over an extramarital affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Germans wrestle with what to do with Hitler's destroyed Eagle's Nest retreat
candidates.description: While some believe the site should be partially or completely rebuilt, others want it abandoned and all memory of its Nazi past forgotten.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay
candidates.description: The culture secretary confirms reports they could be in the list of platforms set to be banned next March.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?
candidates.description: Nintendo has released its remake of what is considered one of the best games ever made - the BBC's Tom Gerken gives his verdict.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Birds return to waterfowl park after oil vandalism
candidates.description: The vandalism of a nearby home heating oil tank resulted in the death of 13 birds from the park.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Rising cost of living tests UK's net zero ambitions
candidates.description: From floods to wildfires to heatwaves, 2026 is the year it became hard to ignore the impact of climate change on UK weather. But will soaring living costs affect the government’s commitment to tackling climate change?
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: France accuses Iran of cyber 'sabotage' in fridge attacks
candidates.description: France says Iranian military hackers took over refrigeration controllers at around 700 different retail sites last month, turning up temperatures in the middle of the night and spoiling millions of dollars' worth of food.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Thick smog shrouds New Delhi after Diwali firecrackers add to seasonal pollution
candidates.description: New Delhi, home to over 30 million people, regularly ranks among the world's most polluted areas during winter, with pollution worsening in late October and November.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: British comedian Russell Brand sentenced to over 10 years for rape and sexual assault
candidates.description: Russell Brand, who became a celebrity darling in the early 2000s, was found guilty on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault in a case brought by six women.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Congress is back after GOP's midterm defeat. And, Trump appoints new chief of staff
candidates.description: Republicans have just weeks left of control of Congress. Here's what to expect. And, Trump has appointed Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff, signaling his readiness to confront his opposition.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Why a South Korean city is turning to a U.S. college to outsmart AI?
candidates.description: Through civic participation and liberal education, South Korean educators hope to "quietly stitch the fabric of our democracy…before it unravels beyond repair."
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: How a bank collapse left millions in limbo and toppled Paraguay's president
candidates.description: A bank's collapse in Paraguay left millions locked out of their money, toppled the president and exposed a web of political and financial ties.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: The world's largest telecoms firm is on trial and the outcome has global implications
candidates.description: Huawei, the world's biggest telecommunications company, is on trial in New York, accused of stealing American technology and evading US sanctions.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Trying to find true owners, Paris' Musee D'Orsay exhibits art looted by Nazis
candidates.description: A new permanent exhibition at Paris' Musee d'Orsay showcases works of art suspected to have been looted by Nazis during the Second World War in France. Experts are trying to find the true owners or their descendants.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Europe to join U.S.-brokered Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, defying Kremlin objections
candidates.description: France says European officials will attend this week's U.S.-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, the first three-way round of negotiations since February.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: No clear winner in New Zealand election, as leaders prepare for weeks of talks
candidates.description: Prime Minister Christopher Luxon, who will lead a caretaker government while negotiations take place, said: "I think everyone's over politics so let's all have a bit of a break for the next three weeks".
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Nvidia shares tumble as the company says it's investigating CEO Jensen Huang
candidates.description: Nvidia's share price falls after the company begins an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's alleged relationship with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: The business of El Niño
candidates.description: El Niño is expected to bring wild weather, but it's also business opportunity for some. Contractors are booked up as homeowners prepare for heavy rains and ski resorts gear up to cash in on snow.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Democrats won big. Can they lower your grocery bill?
candidates.description: Affordability concerns were top of mind for voters heading into the midterms, as tariffs and the war in Iran drove up prices, including food costs. Now, Americans are expecting relief from Washington.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: He was diagnosed with cancer. Then he was told he lost his Medicaid
candidates.description: Health clinics and organizations advocating for poor and working-class Nebraskans say the rollout of Medicaid work requirements has been rife with problems.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: One air ambulance service rethinks what it takes to practice medicine in the sky
candidates.description: Air medical service comes with high risks, high costs, and staffing struggles. To reduce turnover and serve rural patients, LifeFlight of Maine is putting the needs of healthcare workers first.
candidates.author: NPR
